questions.prompt: How does being tired affect your driving?
choices: It slows your reaction to hazards.
It sharpens your focus for a short while.
It matters only late at night.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and drowsiness affect your vision and increase your reaction time to hazards.

questions.prompt: For push/pull steering, where should your hands start on the wheel?
choices: Both hands at the top of the wheel.
questions.explanation: For hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering, start at 9 and 3 or 8 and 4 o'clock.

questions.prompt: When turning with push/pull steering, should your hands cross over the middle of the wheel?
choices: Yes, once for every full turn.
questions.explanation: In push/pull steering your hands never cross the middle of the wheel, and they stay in position even when turning.

questions.prompt: When should you use hand-over-hand steering?
choices: When changing lanes at freeway speed.
When backing up and looking behind you.
When parking or turning at low speed.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering for low-speed turns, parking, or recovering from a skid. When turning while backing, steer with one hand at 12 o'clock.

questions.prompt: You are turning while backing up and looking behind you. Where may you place one hand on the wheel?
questions.explanation: When turning while backing, you may steer with one hand at the 12 o'clock position so you can look behind you.

questions.prompt: When is it acceptable to steer with one hand while driving forward?
choices: When you must work a vehicle control.
On long, straight stretches of freeway.
questions.explanation: Keep both hands on the wheel whenever possible. One hand is acceptable while operating a control that needs a hand off the wheel.

questions.prompt: You are about to change lanes on an empty road. What should you do about signaling?
choices: Signal anyway before you move over.
Skip it; no one is there to see.
Signal only if a car comes into view.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, even when you don't see other vehicles around you.

questions.prompt: When should you use hand-and-arm signals in a car?
choices: Only when you are riding a bicycle or motorcycle.
When your signal lights don't work or are hard to see.
At night, so drivers can see what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Use hand-and-arm signals if your signal lights aren't working or bright sunlight makes them hard to see.

questions.prompt: The driver ahead holds an arm straight out of their window. What are they about to do?
questions.explanation: An arm held straight out signals a left turn.

questions.prompt: The driver ahead holds an arm out of their window, bent up at the elbow. What are they about to do?
questions.explanation: An arm held out and bent up at the elbow signals a right turn.

questions.prompt: The driver ahead holds an arm out of their window, bent down at the elbow. What are they about to do?
questions.explanation: An arm bent down at the elbow means the driver is slowing down or stopping.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist ahead holds one arm straight out to the side, pointing. What does it mean?
choices: They want you to pass them.
They plan to turn that way.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may signal a turn by holding an arm straight out, pointing in the direction they plan to turn.

questions.prompt: On a freeway, what is the least time you should signal before changing lanes?
questions.explanation: Signal before every lane change, and on a freeway signal at least five seconds before you move over.

questions.prompt: Should you signal before pulling away from the curb?
choices: Only if a car is coming.
No, signals are only for turns.
questions.explanation: Signal before pulling next to the curb or away from it.

questions.prompt: You plan to turn into a driveway just past an intersection. When should you signal?
choices: When you are almost through the intersection.
Just before you enter the intersection.
Only once you start to turn into it.
questions.explanation: Signal when you are almost through the intersection, so drivers don't think you are turning at it.

questions.prompt: On a narrow mountain road, below what sight distance ahead should you sound your horn?
questions.explanation: On narrow mountain roads, use your horn to alert oncoming traffic when you can't see at least 200 feet ahead.

questions.prompt: When should you use your horn?
choices: To tell a slow driver to hurry up.
To show another driver you are upset.
To warn others of a hazard.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to let others know you are there, to warn of a hazard, or to avoid a collision.

questions.prompt: What is the closest you may follow another vehicle with your high beams on?
questions.explanation: Dim your high beams within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following, and within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.prompt: What is the rule for driving with only your parking lights on?
choices: It is allowed until 30 minutes after sunset.
It is allowed in light rain.
questions.explanation: Driving with only your parking lights on is illegal at any time. In rain, and from 30 minutes after sunset, use your headlights.

questions.prompt: You must use your headlights when it is too dark to see how far ahead?
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when it is too dark to see from 1,000 feet away.

questions.prompt: What is the latest after sunset you may turn on your headlights?
questions.explanation: Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.prompt: You turn on your wipers because of rain during the day. What else must you do?
choices: Nothing more, since it is daytime.
questions.explanation: If you need your wipers because of fog, rain or snow, you must turn on your low-beam headlights.

questions.prompt: On a sunny day, where should you still use your headlights?
choices: Only where a sign says headlights must be on.
In tunnels and on mountain roads.
Only when you need your wipers.
questions.explanation: Use headlights on mountain roads and in tunnels, even on sunny days.

questions.prompt: You see a crash ahead and need to warn drivers behind you. What can you do?
choices: Tap your brakes three or four times.
Brake hard so they notice your lights.
questions.explanation: Warn drivers behind you by tapping your brakes three or four times, turning on your flashers, or using a hand signal as you slow.

questions.prompt: Your car is failing and you can't get it fully off the road. Where should you stop?
choices: Where drivers behind can see you.
Just past the top of a hill.
Just around a curve, out of sight.
questions.explanation: Stop where people behind you can see you. Never stop just over a hill or around a curve, where drivers may not see you in time.

questions.prompt: You must stop for car trouble, and your car has no emergency flashers. How can you warn others?
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers, or your turn signals if the car doesn't have flashers.
